result: Of 627 consecutive ME/CFS patients on a 10-min 70-degree tilt, 155 (25%) met POTS criteria; median time to HR criteria was 3 min, so a 2-min tilt would miss 55% (95% CI 48-63%) of POTS cases, with no difference by sex, age, duration or hypocapnia.

result: In 43 Fukuda CFS vs 27 controls at 3T, T1-weighted spin-echo signal was lower in a brainstem region (cluster P_FWE=0.002) and higher in bilateral sensorimotor white matter, with brainstem and sensorimotor signal correlated; VBM showed no volume differences.
reason: Altered brainstem MRI signal in a separate cohort; same Barnden/Griffith group already noted as not fully independent

result: VBM in 43 CFS vs 27 controls found no group differences in regional grey or white matter volume, although T1wSE signal intensity differed in brainstem and sensorimotor white matter.

result: Meta-analysis of odds ratios found PEM 10.4 times more likely to be associated with an ME/CFS diagnosis than control status, with recruitment strategy and control selection moderating effect size.

result: In 48 CFS vs 20 sedentary controls (and 27 Sjogren's), plasma cortisol before and after 0.5 mg overnight dexamethasone did not differ from controls, and ex vivo dex suppression of LPS-induced TNF-alpha was reduced rather than enhanced; childhood adversity correlated with cortisol and GR function.
reason: Tests dexamethasone suppression directly and finds no exaggerated cortisol suppression (and reduced ex vivo GR sensitivity)

result: In 107 female CFS patients vs 59 controls the salivary cortisol awakening response was lower (4.2 vs 6.1 nmol/L, p=0.036), daily salivary output did not differ, and hair cortisol trended lower in 46 vs 46 (3.8 vs 4.3 pg/mg, p=0.062).
reason: Same measures (salivary CAR, hair cortisol), same direction, not in finding_studies
